$comment: What to capture out of the Figma file, for `bun run capture:figma`.
`w`/`h` are the size of the node that `node` selects, in design px. They are
load-bearing: the crop scores candidate selection outlines by how close they
are to these numbers and takes the best one, so a wrong size here does not
fail — it returns a different region of canvas and ships it. Two entries in
this table once carried a size that was not their node's, and both shipped.
See docs/decisions/0007 and the SKILL.md in packages/figma-to-site.
Read these numbers off a Figma size badge or a frame's own dimensions. Never
infer one from how a downscaled reference PNG looks.
`note` is prose for humans and agents; the tooling ignores it. Every number
that has a story keeps it here, next to the number.

targets.name: Header
targets.note: 1-122 is the green band, not the hero image: it is 1200x362 and the laptop sits on top of it, overhanging 139px above its top edge and clipped where the band ends. The band is a flat colour reproduced in CSS by components/sections/Header.tsx, so what this exports is the laptop alone, measured off design/refs/Header.png. Declaring 1200x362 and taking the selection itself is what shipped the band as the hero asset.

targets.name: Showcase
targets.note: 1200x664.29, per the size badge Figma printed beside this selection. It was briefly changed to 704 on the theory that the section reference (design/refs/ShowcaseImage.png, 1200x704) *was* this node, because at thumbnail size the image looks like it fills that frame corner to corner. It does not: there is 20px of white above and below it. The 704 crop reached past the node, caught the selection outline and the badge, and shipped them — which is how the true size became legible. The block check did not notice, because a 237x34 badge barely moves a 48-cell grid; assertNoViewerChrome is the check that does.

targets.name: CenteredCta
targets.note: 462, not the 464 originally declared: the selection outline the capture actually matched measures 1197x461 at 2x. Two px is inside every tolerance here, but a declared size that disagrees with the outline is the exact discrepancy that shipped wrong assets, so it is not left standing.

targets.name: Footer
targets.note: 1200x250, per the size badge Figma printed beside the selection in the original capture — which declared 519, matched nothing, and cropped a strip of Figma's own UI into design/refs/Footer.png as a design *reference*.
